references.title: Understanding lifetimes and failure modes of defective washing machines and dishwashers
references.scope_note: Published analysis of about 11,000 diagnoses from an independent European repair centre. Supports fault-family coverage only; not a target-market prevalence distribution or a calibrated washer prior.

references.title: Design for repair: insights to develop functional modules in household appliances
references.scope_note: Physical disassembly and functional-module analysis across cooking-appliance categories. Useful methodology reference; conclusions do not automatically transfer to washers.

references.title: Symtropy washer reference architecture and benchmark protocol
references.scope_note: Project-defined protocol and hard safety/function claim boundaries; not a physical measurement or product qualification.

tasks.fault_family: User-accessible drain filter or foreign-object blockage
tasks.observed_symptom: Cycle ends or pauses with poor draining; water remains in the drum or drainage is slow.
competing_hypotheses: Accessible filter obstructed by coins/lint/foreign object
Drain hose restriction or installation issue
Pump fault or internal blockage requiring qualified service
Water-level sensing/control issue
safe_discriminating_checks: Use only the model's approved user isolation and water-capture procedure; inspect and clean the accessible filter.
Observe whether the approved user maintenance resolves draining; if not, stop and refer rather than assume the pump is faulty.
Record symptom, visible debris, water handling and approved instructions used; no exposed or energized internals.
repair_scope_options: Clean the intended user-accessible filter and remove an accessible foreign object
Qualified inspection and repair of drain hose/pump path
Replace a pump assembly only after model-specific diagnosis supports that scope
tasks.hazard_boundary: User scope is limited to the documented accessible filter/drain maintenance with instructed isolation and water capture; internal pump, mains and powered tests remain qualified service.
post_repair_verification: Approved drain function check with all covers/filters restored
Leak observation after reassembly or user maintenance as specified by the manual
Record recurrence status at the declared follow-up point
tasks.recurrence_policy: No claim of success without a completed approved drain check; recurrence remains pending until the named follow-up window is complete.

tasks.fault_family: Door closure, interlock or door-seal problem
tasks.observed_symptom: Door will not close/start the cycle, or water is observed around the door seal.
competing_hypotheses: Laundry/object obstructs closure or door alignment is poor
Door seal is dirty, displaced or damaged
Interlock/lock actuator fault
Leak has another source and is misattributed to the door
safe_discriminating_checks: Perform visual inspection and user-approved cleaning/obstruction checks without removing protective parts.
Compare the symptom with the model-specific indicator/manual diagnostic tree; a code alone is not confirmation.
Qualified service distinguishes lock/harness/control hypotheses using the approved isolated procedure.
repair_scope_options: Remove obstruction or clean an intended user-accessible seal surface
Qualified seal or lock-assembly repair/replacement
Larger assembly replacement only where diagnosis and parts architecture justify it
tasks.hazard_boundary: Internal door-lock electrical work is qualified service; never bypass the interlock. User instructions may cover only visible inspection/cleaning allowed by the manual.
post_repair_verification: Door closure/interlock behaviour under the approved guarded test
Leak check under the model-specific procedure
Record any interlock/bypass attempt as a critical safety failure
tasks.recurrence_policy: A successful repair requires the interlock/closure function and required leak checks; repeat failures are tracked through a declared observation window.

tasks.fault_family: Drain path, pump or pump-drive fault
tasks.observed_symptom: Drain failure persists after approved user-accessible filter cleaning or is accompanied by abnormal pump behaviour.
competing_hypotheses: Downstream hose/path blockage
Pump impeller or pump assembly fault
Pump power/drive/controller fault
Incorrect water-level state or sensor issue
safe_discriminating_checks: Confirm documented external hose routing and approved accessible-filter result before escalating the hypothesis.
Qualified technician performs approved isolated checks to separate path obstruction, pump, drive and sensing hypotheses.
Preserve original symptom and test results; do not convert missing readings into a failed pump diagnosis.
repair_scope_options: Clear a confirmed serviceable path obstruction
Replace a proven failed pump or serviceable pump subcomponent when supported
Replace the larger pump/control assembly only if diagnosis and availability justify it
tasks.hazard_boundary: Internal wet/mains work and any powered tests are qualified, guarded and product-specific; no energizing opened equipment or defeating protection.
post_repair_verification: Approved drain performance test with enclosure/guards restored
Leak and protective-electrical checks as required by the model-specific repair procedure
Document actual installed part and post-check result
tasks.recurrence_policy: Failed attempts and rework remain in total restore cost; recurrence is pending until follow-up is complete.

tasks.fault_family: Inlet valve, supply restriction or water-level sensing
tasks.observed_symptom: Filling is slow, absent or inconsistent, or the washer appears to overfill or misjudge water level.
competing_hypotheses: Closed/low-pressure supply or accessible inlet-screen restriction
Inlet valve fault
Pressure/water-level sensor, hose or harness fault
Controller/programme condition mistaken for a part failure
safe_discriminating_checks: Check external tap/hose conditions and user-accessible inlet screens only where the manual permits, with supply isolated.
Qualified service distinguishes valve response from pressure sensing, harness and control behaviour using approved tests.
Record supply condition and instrument status; a reading outside calibration/range is unknown, not a zero or confirmed component fault.
repair_scope_options: Correct external supply or clean an intended accessible inlet screen
Qualified replacement of confirmed valve, sensor or harness component
Larger assembly replacement only when evidence and part economics support it
tasks.hazard_boundary: Internal valve/sensor/harness work involves water and potentially mains-adjacent components; qualified isolation and post-repair leak/electrical checks are required.
post_repair_verification: Approved fill/level-control cycle check
Leak check and required electrical/protective checks
Confirm the original symptom is resolved under a declared programme and supply condition
tasks.recurrence_policy: Record full supply conditions and follow-up state; do not attribute external supply recurrence to the product without evidence.

tasks.observed_symptom: Excessive movement, noise or imbalance appears during spin or load transitions.
competing_hypotheses: Uneven load or unsuitable installation/levelling
Worn shock absorber/suspension or mounting component
Bearing/drum damage or structural looseness
Control/speed feedback issue
safe_discriminating_checks: Use the model's user guidance to check load distribution and accessible installation/levelling conditions first.
Qualified inspection distinguishes suspension wear from bearing, drum, mount and feedback hypotheses with the machine de-energized as required.
Record noise/vibration method, load and cycle state; do not conduct exposed or unguarded spin trials.
repair_scope_options: Correct load/installation condition where applicable
Qualified replacement of confirmed suspension/mounting wear items
Major tub/drum repair only if diagnosed; compare bearing/tub repair against assembly replacement
tasks.hazard_boundary: Internal suspension and drum work involves heavy, spring-loaded or rotating assemblies; use qualified personnel, supports/lifting procedures, guards and approved post-repair test.
post_repair_verification: Guarded approved vibration/spin test under a declared load
Check fasteners, mounts and clearances under product-specific procedure
Record noise/vibration and recurrence during defined follow-up
tasks.recurrence_policy: Repeat abnormal vibration after repair is recurrence/rework, not a new clean pass; follow-up window and load conditions are recorded.

tasks.fault_family: Heater, temperature sensing or thermal-control fault
tasks.observed_symptom: Cycle behaviour or wash result suggests temperature performance differs from the declared programme, or a thermal fault is reported.
competing_hypotheses: Selected programme and supply conditions explain observed temperature
Temperature sensor or harness fault
Heater element fault
Control/relay/drive fault
safe_discriminating_checks: Check programme/settings and user-visible messages against the manual before assuming a hardware failure.
Qualified technician follows approved isolation/discharge and measurement procedures to discriminate sensor, heater and control hypotheses.
Do not probe exposed energized mains or treat an uncalibrated temperature/electrical measurement as evidence.
repair_scope_options: Correct settings/use misunderstanding where supported by evidence
Qualified repair or replacement of a confirmed sensor/harness/heater component
Replace a larger control/heater assembly only when justified by diagnosis and lifecycle cost
tasks.hazard_boundary: Heater, mains, stored energy and thermal hazards require qualified isolation, product-specific procedures and prescribed post-repair electrical and thermal checks.
post_repair_verification: Validated programme-specific temperature/function check using suitable calibrated measurement
Required protective electrical/insulation/earth checks under applicable service procedure
Verify the declared cycle completes with required user-visible behaviour
tasks.recurrence_policy: Successful status requires the defined temperature/function receipt and applicable safety check; recurrence cannot be inferred from one display state.

tasks.fault_family: Drive, motor, speed feedback or control electronics
tasks.observed_symptom: Drum fails to agitate or spin as expected, or motion is intermittent/abnormal.
competing_hypotheses: Belt/coupling or mechanical transmission fault where the architecture uses one
Motor or motor-winding/component fault
Speed feedback/tachometer/sensor or harness fault
Inverter/drive board/control fault
safe_discriminating_checks: Identify the selected physical drive architecture and check permitted user-visible diagnostics before inferring a failed motor.
Qualified technician uses the approved isolated sequence to distinguish mechanical, motor, feedback and drive electronics faults.
Log exact firmware/configuration and component IDs; do not use a live exposed-drive experiment or bypass an interlock.
repair_scope_options: Replace a confirmed belt/coupling or other separately serviceable mechanical part
Replace a proven motor/feedback/sensor component
Replace a drive/controller module only when the diagnosis, repairability and stock cost support that scope
tasks.hazard_boundary: Drive, motor and power electronics work is qualified service; no open-guard powered testing, interlock bypass or unqualified stored-energy handling.
post_repair_verification: Approved guarded agitation/spin test using declared load and programme
Required post-repair protective/electrical checks
Record noise, speed/operation and actual assembly/parts consumed
tasks.recurrence_policy: Track rework and return failures separately by installed part and procedure revision; follow-up remains pending until its declared window completes.

tasks.observed_symptom: Persistent rumble, drum play, leakage or mechanical symptoms remain after easier external causes are excluded.
competing_hypotheses: Foreign object or local contact mistaken for bearing damage
Suspension/mounting or shaft issue
Bearing/seal wear
Tub/drum structural damage or assembly misalignment
safe_discriminating_checks: Start with an approved de-energized inspection that separates obvious foreign objects, external contact and suspension concerns.
Qualified inspection measures play, sealing/surface condition and relevant assembly tolerances using an appropriate support fixture.
Record what evidence supports bearing-only versus tub/drum replacement; do not choose scope based solely on expected lower labour.
repair_scope_options: Remove a confirmed foreign object or correct a separately serviceable non-bearing part
Replace a separately serviceable bearing/seal unit in an architecture designed and qualified for it
Replace a bolted tub/drum or larger assembly when repairability, seal integrity, structure or tolerance requires it
tasks.hazard_boundary: Heavy tub/drum disassembly entails crush, lifting, stored spring and rotating hazards; use qualified staff, reviewed support fixtures, guards and product-specific safety checks.
post_repair_verification: Static leak/seal integrity check followed by required controlled cycle checks
Guarded, approved vibration/spin check and relevant temperature/noise observations
Record assembly tolerances, fasteners/seal handling, discarded mass and follow-up recurrence
tasks.recurrence_policy: A repaired bearing is not proven durable by a single spin; record test exposure and recurrence window, including seal leaks, noise and rework.
